To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most common approach for product recognition is to use deep convolutional neural networks.
the existing studies are classified into four main categories: 1) Product recognition, 2) Planogram matching, 3) Product counting and 4) Shelf layout.

(1) the existing methods are based on a variety of features, (2) the existing methods have been tested on different datasets, (3) there are different approaches for training the classifiers, (4) the existing works use different classifiers for classification, (5) the existing works have different performance metrics and (6) the existing methods can be classified as either 2D or 3D methods
In summary, our research is concerned with
a survey of existing works and a discussion of the open problems.
a survey of the literature on shelf image-based product recognition.
the following questions: (i) What is product recognition? (ii) What are the methods of product recognition? (iii) What is the state of the art in product recognition?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is still a need for an autonomous system which can perform the tasks mentioned above.
there is no single method which is capable of recognizing all the products in the literature.
the existing studies can be classified as shelf detection, product detection, product recognition and product tracking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most common approach in the literature is to use a combination of color and edge information.
the most important features are color and texture, the most common methods are color histogram, SIFT and HOG and the most common classifiers are SVM and kNN.
the existing studies have focused on the product recognition problem in the context of merchandising.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existing works are mainly focused on the recognition of products on shelves.
most of the works have been carried out on the same dataset.
the existing studies are not able to address all problems in merchandising and that there is still a significant need for research in this field.
